title: Database Integration Concepts
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of database integration concepts using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates database integration concepts.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Database Integration Concepts** as part of **Serialization, Networking, and Application Integration**. Integration code must validate external data, handle timeouts and failure states, keep credentials outside source control, and test boundary behavior. Use the subtopics—Relational Data and Object Models, Connection and Transaction Basics, Database Access Layers—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it

items.title: Relational Data and Object Models
items.text: Relational Data and Object Models should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Connection and Transaction Basics
items.text: Connection and Transaction Basics is one part of database integration concepts. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Database Access Layers
items.text: Database Access Layers crosses a system boundary. Model success and failure, validate external data, apply timeout/retry rules deliberately, and keep credentials and database access out of presentation code.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Database Integration Concepts removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
